title: Should, have to, must
point: Should gives advice, have to states a real obligation, must is strong or written, and don't have to means it isn't necessary.

sentences.ja: 今日は早く寝たほうがいいよ。
sentences.text: You should get to bed early tonight.
sentences.note: "Had better" sounds like a warning, so "should" is safer for friendly advice.

sentences.ja: 明日は朝六時に起きなきゃいけないんだ。
sentences.text: I have to get up at six tomorrow.

sentences.ja: 急がなくていいよ、時間はたっぷりあるから。
sentences.text: You don't have to rush. We've got plenty of time.
sentences.note: "Don't have to" means it's not needed; "mustn't" would forbid it.

sentences.ja: このことは誰にも言っちゃダメだよ。
sentences.text: You can't tell anyone about this, okay?
sentences.note: In speech, "can't" is the usual way to forbid something; "mustn't" sounds formal or British.

sentences.ja: その件、上司に相談したほうがいいと思う。
sentences.text: I think you should talk to your boss about it.
sentences.note: Wrapping "should" in "I think" makes the advice sound less pushy.

sentences.ja: 昨日は残業しなきゃいけなかった。
sentences.text: I had to stay late at work yesterday.

sentences.ja: この薬は食後に飲まなければなりません。
sentences.text: You must take this medicine after meals.

sentences.ja: 全部の論文を読む必要はないよ。
sentences.text: You don't have to read every single paper.

sentences.ja: 経費精算は月末までに出さないといけません。
sentences.text: You have to submit your expense report by the end of the month.

sentences.ja: 何時までに着けばいいですか？
sentences.text: What time should I be there by?
sentences.note: English uses "should" here; a literal "is it good if" sounds odd.
